description: Change the data itself: INSERT adds rows, UPDATE changes them, DELETE removes them — always with a WHERE clause.

screens.body:
Until now every query was read-only. INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE WRITE — they change what's stored. This is the powerful, scary part of SQL.

Rule one: SELECT can't hurt you; these three can. In real work you'll run them on test data first. Here you'll practice them safely in JavaScript: push(), map(), and filter().
screens.heading: Reading vs writing

screens.body:
INSERT adds a new row. Name the table, name the columns, give the values: INSERT INTO students (name, program, gpa) VALUES ('Zainab', 'Data Science', 3.4).

Values line up with columns in order. Skip a column and it gets NULL (if the table allows it). In JavaScript, this is push() on the array.

check.question: The VALUES for a new student named Zainab:

screens.heading: INSERT adds rows
screens.keyPoint: INSERT = name columns, give values, in order.

screens.body:
UPDATE changes existing rows — but ONLY the ones WHERE catches. UPDATE students SET gpa = 2.9 WHERE id = 6 fixes Noah's GPA.

SET names the change, WHERE names the target. Forget the WHERE and EVERY row gets the new value. That mistake has a name among developers: 'the oops update.' Always write WHERE first.

check.question: UPDATE students SET gpa = 2.9 WHERE id = 6 changes…

screens.heading: UPDATE changes rows
screens.keyPoint: UPDATE without WHERE changes EVERY row.

screens.body:
DELETE removes rows — again, only the ones WHERE catches. DELETE FROM students WHERE gpa < 2.5 removes Noah (2.4).

There is no undo button for DELETE. In real databases, developers delete from a copy first, or SELECT with the same WHERE to preview what they're about to remove. In JavaScript, this is filter() keeping the rows you want.

check.question: DELETE FROM students WHERE gpa < 2.5 removes…

screens.heading: DELETE removes rows
screens.keyPoint: DELETE without WHERE wipes the whole table.

screens.body:
The same WHERE you learned for SELECT protects your writes. Pick your targets with SELECT + WHERE first — look at them — then run the UPDATE or DELETE with the identical WHERE.

Write it as a habit: SELECT preview → UPDATE/DELETE. It takes five seconds and saves careers.

options: SELECT with the same WHERE first
check.question: Before running DELETE, you should…

screens.heading: The safe-write habit

screens.body:
You can UPDATE or INSERT based on more than one condition: SET gpa = gpa + 0.1 WHERE program = 'Network Security' bumps every Network Security GPA by 0.1.

Values on the right can use math or the old value — gpa + 0.1 means 'the current GPA, plus 0.1.' In JavaScript that's a map() that tweaks matching objects.

options: Every Network Security student's GPA rises by 0.1
check.question: SET gpa = gpa + 0.1 WHERE program = 'Network Security' does what?

code.snippet:
UPDATE students
SET gpa = gpa + 0.1
WHERE program = 'Network Security';
-- Tega: 3.2 -> 3.3, Noah: 2.4 -> 2.5

screens.heading: UPDATE with expressions
screens.keyPoint: SET can use the old value in math.

screens.body:
The SQL playground doesn't run writes against a real database — so you'll simulate: INSERT = push() a new object, UPDATE = map() and change the matching one, DELETE = filter() keeping what stays.

The logic is identical; only the tool differs. Master WHERE in SELECT and you've already mastered the targeting of every write.
screens.heading: Practice writes safely in JS
screens.keyPoint: push() inserts, map() updates, filter() deletes.
